model.unique_candidate_set: Cset = H(DomainSuite || generation || predecessor_digest || EncodePF(sorted(unique dc)))
model.question: When two distinct observations have equal canonical candidate content, should uniqueness be defined by content identity or by observation-instance identity?

identity_policy_tests.result: pass only when candidate semantics are content-equivalence classes
identity_policy_tests.reason: Two equal canonical contents intentionally collapse to one dc, so strict unique-set rejection prevents multiplicity from changing selection. This is deterministic and duplicate-injection resistant, but it cannot prove that two independent observations occurred.

identity_policy_tests.result: preserves distinct instances but introduces identity trust surface
identity_policy_tests.reason: Distinct CanonicalInstanceID values keep otherwise identical observations separate. This is correct only when instance identity is itself semantically relevant and canonically/verifiably assigned. If producers can mint arbitrary IDs, multiplicity inflation merely moves from duplicate digests to Sybil instance creation.

identity_policy_tests.result: best separation for the tested evidence-handoff model
identity_policy_tests.reason: Keep candidate selection keyed by unique dc while separately committing each observation record in Robs. Selection therefore cannot be multiplicity-weighted by duplicate observations, yet replay can verify that multiple observation instances were presented, subject to the unresolved authenticity of instance/provenance fields.

If candidate ranking, tie-break, sampling, or weighting consumes raw observation count without an explicit evidence-weight model, equal-content duplicates can alter the useful outcome and violate the unique-set semantics established in p1-sa-599.
A nonce, timestamp, repository path, or producer-chosen UUID can make encodings unique without proving distinct real observations. Replayability of bytes is not authenticity of provenance.

result.observation: Content identity and observation-instance identity are different semantic layers. A single candidate_digest cannot safely serve both if the selector wants unique content while the evidence package must preserve repeated or independently sourced observations.
result.inference: For the exact tested evidence-handoff model, candidate_digest should bind canonical candidate content only, while a separate raw-observation commitment binds content_digest plus canonical instance/provenance fields. Bind instance identity into the candidate digest only when the downstream decision rule explicitly treats distinct instances as distinct candidates and the identity issuance/authentication rule is independently defined and Sybil-resistant. This separation preserves deterministic unique-set selection without erasing observation multiplicity.
result.package_completeness: pass for the narrow representation-layer separation only: Cset proves the unique content candidates presented to selection, while Robs can commit the raw observation layer. It does not prove that instance identifiers or provenance are truthful.
result.replayability: pass for deterministic byte-level replay of both layers given canonical encodings. Authentic replay of who/what produced each observation remains unresolved without a trust/authentication mechanism.
result.hidden_executor_absence: pass for this exact symbolic slice: local deterministic reasoning plus lightweight repository state/evidence transport only
result.quota_zero_assessment: The representation/replay rule requires no hosted runner, Codespaces, cloud compute/storage, paid API/model, artifact service, or finite credit. Repository APIs are used only as lightweight durable transport; rate-limit recovery remains cross-invocation.
result.conflict_check: CLEAN-safe: semantically consumed only frozen sanitized controls and own scientist_agents LATEST/p1-sa-599. No O-derived, downstream, other-worker, shared-ledger, protected-primary, manual-user, or scheduler semantics were used.
